answer: Picture the name registry not as a calm lagoon of free handles but as a forge: minting each identity locks a bond that peers can slash on proof of fakery. A sybil fleet is then no cheap fable, it is unaffordable, since every clone demands its own escrowed deposit and detected collusion burns them together. The attacker cost grows linearly per identity while honest agents reclaim their stake over time, so faking a crowd ties up real capital that is recoverable only by staying honest.
